units.why: Instructors state the allowed or limited use course by course, so the decision of what AI use is allowed is left to the faculty member, 'any allowed or limited use ... within the course'; the university sets no rule itself, so P04 (instructor sets the rule).

units.passage: UTA supports faculty choice: AI use may be restricted, guided, or integrated depending on disciplinary context and course goals.
units.why: "UTA supports faculty choice: AI use may be restricted, guided, or integrated" leaves the stance to faculty and names three levels; P04 (who decides) is the primary fit, with the levels a secondary feature of P05.
units.fit_note: Also names three modes (restricted, guided, integrated) that resemble tiers (P05).

units.passage: this post focuses on clarity, transparency, and assignment‑specific AI policies .
units.why: A blog recap says it focuses on 'clarity, transparency, and assignment-specific AI policies'; it endorses setting AI rules per assignment, P04.

units.passage: Every syllabus must include a course AI policy that designates whether AI is permitted, prohibited, or partially permitted, with clear conditions for use.
units.policy: Each course's AI policy designates whether AI is permitted, prohibited, or partially permitted, with clear conditions for use.
units.why: The same sentence requires the policy to 'designate whether AI is permitted, prohibited, or partially permitted', leaving the choice to each course; I chose P04 (each instructor sets the rule) over P05 because the three categories are what the instructor selects, not a defined tier scheme with named levels.
units.fit_note: Also names three categories of use (P05) without defining tiers.

units.passage: Suggested options are provided below; faculty are also welcome to write their own statements
units.why: Faculty may write their own statements instead of the supplied options: 'faculty are also welcome to write their own statements'. The decision about the course AI rule rests with the instructor, so P04.

units.passage: Artificial intelligence (AI) may be used for [assignment types A, B & C] with appropriate citation, but not for [assignment types D, E & F]
units.policy: AI may be used for the assignment types the instructor lists, with appropriate citation, but not for the other listed assignment types.
units.why: Option B allows AI for some assignment types and not others: 'may be used for [assignment types A, B & C] with appropriate citation, but not for [assignment types D, E & F]'. Use is decided assignment by assignment, P04; no AI-use categories are named beyond assignment type.
units.fit_note: Template for a limited-use policy; P05 also fits as the middle tier.

units.passage: Faculty have the freedom and responsibility to determine how generative AI can be used in academic work under faculty supervision.
units.why: "Faculty have the freedom and responsibility to determine how generative AI can be used" hands the decision to instructors rather than setting a university rule (P04).

units.passage: Faculty have the discretion to permit, prohibit, or partially allow the use of generative AI.
units.why: "Faculty have the discretion to permit, prohibit, or partially allow" gives the decision per instructor (P04). The three options look like tiers (P05), but they are not defined levels, so P04 fits better.
units.fit_note: Also names three categories (permit, partial, prohibit), which touches P05; the rule coded is faculty discretion.

units.passage: Whether you plan to fully embrace AI in your course, allow limited use, or prohibit it altogether, communicate your rationale clearly
units.why: The opening says faculty may 'fully embrace AI in your course, allow limited use, or prohibit it altogether', so the decision is left to each instructor. P04 fits because the choice is per course; modality may because it permits instructors to choose.

units.passage: Define which assignments or process stages explicitly prohibit AI use.
units.why: 'Define which assignments or process stages explicitly prohibit AI use' tells instructors to mark per-assignment bans, so the rule is set per assignment (P04).

units.passage: UTHealth Houston and McGovern Medical School do not expressly prohibit the use of AI tools like ChatGPT and others, leaving faculty and departments to determine how it may or may not be used in classes, educational programs, and so on.
units.why: The policy says 'UTHealth Houston and McGovern Medical School do not expressly prohibit' AI, 'leaving faculty and departments to determine how it may or may not be used'; this hands the decision to faculty and departments, so P04 (instructor and department level), not P85.
units.fit_note: Also states there is no express prohibition at university or school level. Also leaves the decision to departments, not only instructors (P85).

units.passage: Faculty are strongly encouraged to develop their own policies regulating the use of generative AI tools in their courses, including allowing or disallowing some or all uses of such tools.
units.why: "Faculty are strongly encouraged to develop their own policies ... allowing or disallowing some or all uses" leaves the AI rule to instructors, so P04 (not P02, since no default stance is set).

units.passage: completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor
units.policy: ChatGPT or similar AI Tools must not be used for completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor.
units.why: 'completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor' bans AI use for coursework beyond what the instructor allows; the rule is tied to the instructor's permission, so P04 with a fit note, actor student, restrict.
units.fit_note: A prohibition on use beyond what the instructor allows; P04 captures instructor control but not the ban. B: the ban depends on what the instructor allows and is framed as non-public output.

units.passage: If generative AI is allowed in a particular course, students must be aware of the following:
units.why: "If generative AI is allowed in a particular course" makes AI permission a course-by-course decision, so P04 (informs).

units.passage: Our approach reflects our commitment to fostering innovation while respecting individual choices.
units.why: "Our approach reflects our commitment to fostering innovation while respecting individual choices" leaves AI decisions to individual faculty, so P04.

units.passage: Faculty are responsible for their syllabus and courses. Because faculty may choose different approaches for generative AI, clearly state in the syllabus and the course homepage whether and how you are allowing the use of AI.
units.policy: Faculty are responsible for their syllabus and courses, and may choose different approaches for generative AI.
units.why: "Faculty are responsible for their syllabus and courses" and "may choose different approaches" means each instructor sets the rule, so P04.

units.passage: You always have control over your course, and you may choose to not use generative AI for your course.
units.why: "You always have control over your course" affirms instructor discretion including opting out, so P04.
units.fit_note: Also says faculty may choose not to use generative AI themselves.

units.passage: Texas State University does not have a policy regarding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the classroom, which provides instructors the academic freedom to determine appropriate use for their own courses
units.why: The page says the university has no AI policy and that this gives instructors "the academic freedom to determine appropriate use for their own courses". The decision is placed with each instructor, which is P04, not a default stance.

units.passage: Whether this violates the Honor Code policy will depend on the professor’s course policy.
units.why: Makes the violation question depend on the professor's course policy, a per-instructor rule, P04.

units.passage: Examples of AI-generated content include, but are not limited to: proprietary or unpublished research legal analysis or advice decision making in the recruitment of personnel or disciplinary action completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor
units.why: "completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor" appears in a list of AI-generated content users answer for, so students are responsible for AI work done outside what the instructor allows: informs, during-work, P04 (instructor decides), unit stance restrict.
units.fit_note: Appears in a list of examples of content users are responsible for, so it is indirect. Appears as a list example, not a freestanding rule.

units.passage: Faculty have the discretion to permit, partially permit, or prohibit the use of generative AI
units.why: The sentence says faculty 'have the discretion to permit, partially permit, or prohibit' AI, so the university sets no rule and hands the decision to instructors; P04 fits because the choice is per instructor.

units.passage: Faculty have the option to allow or prohibit this technology in their courses
units.why: The note-taking section says 'Faculty have the option to allow or prohibit this technology in their courses', leaving AI note-taking to each instructor, P04.

units.passage: generative AI use in this course is not permitted. Do not use generative AI tools or features to create, solve, summarize, translate, revise, or substantially transform work submitted for credit. Basic grammar, spelling, and punctuation features, approved assistive technologies, and approved disability accommodations are permitted unless they generate or substantially rewrite content or replace the skill being assessed. Ask before using an AI tool if you are unsure whether it is permitted. Use of generative AI outside these boundaries may be considered a violation of Texas Tech University’s Academic Integrity Policy. AI Use Permitted To support your development and demonstration of the course learning outcomes, generative AI use in this course is permitted only as specified for each assignment
units.why: The permitted template says AI 'is permitted only as specified for each assignment', so permission is assignment by assignment, P04.

units.passage: You may use generative AI for learning support and planning, such as explaining concepts, generating practice questions, brainstorming ideas, or creating a preliminary outline. You must not include AI-generated language, solutions, analysis, code, media, translations, or revisions in submitted work unless the assignment directions explicitly permit them. You are responsible for ensuring that the central ideas and final work are your own. LEVEL 2 AI-Assisted Collaboration You may use generative AI only for the purposes identified in the assignment directions
units.why: Level 2 allows AI 'only for the purposes identified in the assignment directions', so each assignment names the allowed uses, P04.
units.fit_note: Defines the Level 2 tier; examples include coding support and data exploration. / Examples listed are feedback, revision, translation, coding support, data exploration, media development.
